analysis.title: Third Quarter GDP Growth Accelerated, Underscoring the Economy's Resilience
key_insights: Real GDP rose at an annualized 3.4% in Q3 2026 in the BEA initial estimate, up from 2.2% in Q2 and above PNC's forecast of 3.1%. Real GDP is up 2.8% y/y, from 2.2% in Q2.

Consumer spending grew an annualized 3.8%, unchanged from Q2, and contributed 2.52 points to growth. Services contributed 1.89 points (up from 1.57) and goods 0.63 points (down from 0.94). PNC cites faster real disposable income growth and modest job gains as support.

Gross private domestic investment contributed 3.27 points, up from 0.82 in Q2. Fixed investment added 1.66 points, non-residential spending subtracted 0.12 points, and inventories added 1.61 points, the largest inventory contribution since Q3 2021 (2.16 points).
The three AI-related non-residential categories (information processing equipment, software, R&D) contributed 1.30 points, nearly double the 0.69 points in Q2.
Government spending added 0.90 points. Federal added 0.91 (defense 0.41, non-defense 0.49) and state and local was virtually flat.

Net exports subtracted 3.32 points: imports subtracted 2.64 and exports subtracted 0.68. Imports rose an annualized 19.7% and exports fell 5.7%. The import surge was concentrated in capital goods and tech infrastructure (computers, peripherals, information-processing equipment) for the AI and data center buildout.

Final sales to private domestic purchasers, which excludes net exports, inventories and government, rose at a 4.9% annualized rate, up from 4.6% in Q2. PNC calls it a good measure of underlying demand.
The PCE price index rose 2.1% in Q3, down from 5.0% in Q2. Core PCE slowed to 2.5% from 3.3%.
PNC's baseline is real GDP growth around 2.0% through the second half of next year, mainly from slower consumer and business fixed investment spending.
PNC expects the FOMC to hike the fed funds rate by 25 basis points in December and again in March because of elevated inflation, which would put the rate at 4.25% to 4.50%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Initial BEA estimate, up from 2.2% in Q2 and above PNC's 3.1% forecast. Part of the gain came from inventories, which added 1.61 points.

macro_indicators.interpretation: PNC's pre-release forecast. The actual print beat it by 0.3 points.
Unchanged from Q2 and contributed 2.52 points to growth.
Driven by capital goods and tech infrastructure for the AI and data center buildout. Subtracted 2.64 points from GDP.

macro_indicators.indicator: Final sales to private domestic purchasers (q/q SAAR)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 4.6% in Q2. Indicates strong underlying private demand.
PNC expects a slowdown in consumer and business fixed investment spending.
PNC expects 25 basis point hikes in December and March because of elevated inflation.

risk_factors: Slowing consumer spending and business fixed investment spending are expected to pull growth to around 2.0% through the second half of next year.
Elevated inflation is the reason PNC expects further FOMC rate hikes.
Q3 growth leaned on inventories (1.61 points) and AI-related investment, and net exports subtracted 3.32 points.
